deferred_fields.description: The Jira workflow status tickets transition to after code is committed via PR. Usually auto-resolved.
deferred_fields.guidance: Deferred: usually resolved automatically by the status resolver; set manually only to override.

deferred_fields.description: Cached CI check configuration resolved by the CI resolver agent. Automatically populated.
deferred_fields.guidance: Deferred/server-managed: populated by resolve-ci-checks; do not set during install.

deferred_fields.description: Per-repo control field for the CI follow-up step in implement-ticket and check-ci-ticket pipelines. REPLACE-NOT-AUGMENT: when configured (non-NULL), this owns the CI follow-up step entirely and bypasses the baseline poll-only instruction behavior. When NULL, monitor-ci-checks.md falls back to poll-only defaults (max_iterations=1, max_minutes=10). Stored as JSON text with EXACTLY four keys: strategy, max_iterations, max_minutes, instructions. Unknown keys are rejected with HTTP 422. strategy must be one of 'poll_only' (preserve baseline polling, no fixes), 'fix_and_iterate' (self-contained correction loop), or 'custom' (instructions are the complete CI follow-up instruction set). max_iterations is an integer in [1, 10]. max_minutes is an integer in [1, 120]. Booleans are explicitly rejected for the integer fields. instructions is free-form prose up to 8192 UTF-8 bytes (byte-length, not character count). For strategy='fix_and_iterate', empty instructions is allowed and means the loop uses only structured CI failure signals. For strategy='custom', instructions must be non-empty (whitespace-only is rejected) and is the complete CI follow-up instruction set. Note: 'custom' instructions are authoritative for CI follow-up behavior, but they remain subject to normal tool approval, credential handling, secret-handling, and platform safety constraints — they cannot bypass approval gates, exfiltrate secrets, or otherwise override platform safety policies. Validation runs via the shared validate_ci_followup_config_value helper; valid payloads are persisted as canonical JSON via json.dumps.
deferred_fields.guidance: Deferred policy field: configure the CI follow-up loop intentionally; not a bootstrap field.

deferred_fields.description: Optional plain prose with repository-specific advice for Epic Implementer CI repair (for example how this repository's CI checks relate to local commands). It is added to every CI repair job as untrusted reference material, so it cannot change scope, which checks gate, or verification, commit, and push policy. Up to 8192 UTF-8 bytes, measured on the submitted text and again after secret redaction; oversized or malformed text is rejected, never cut. An empty or whitespace-only value clears the field to NULL.
deferred_fields.guidance: Deferred owner-written field: install must not derive or set it. Owner-provided advice cannot alter scope, gate membership, verification, commit, or push policy.

deferred_fields.description: List of LLM providers permitted for this project, in addition to the primary provider. Accepts a comma-separated string. If empty or null, the project requests its PRIMARY provider only -- it does not mean all providers are allowed. Every provider must be one the owning account's subscription plan entitles.
deferred_fields.guidance: Deferred policy field: restricts which providers automations may use; not a bootstrap field.

deferred_fields.description: Scalar boolean gating whether the final plan reviewer may plan mutating smoke-verification steps against local/ephemeral state only. Accepts a JSON boolean or 'true'/'false'.
deferred_fields.guidance: Deferred policy field: enable mutating smoke verification intentionally; not a bootstrap field.

deferred_fields.description: Nullable boolean opting this repository OUT of Bridge SFCC MCP tool awareness during plan generation and final review. Unset (null) and false both ALLOW awareness — enabling is the default for SFCC platforms, because SFCC tool availability cannot be detected server-side and is therefore assumed. Only the explicit value true disables it, which also suppresses the deterministic SFCC setup-documentation referral. Has no effect on non-SFCC projects, where awareness is already off structurally. Accepts a JSON boolean, 'true'/'false', or blank to clear back to null.
deferred_fields.guidance: Deferred policy field: set to true only when a repo should never be offered Bridge's SFCC metadata tooling; not a bootstrap field.

deferred_fields.description: Scalar boolean gating whether the jira-ticket-writer agent's non-blocking regression-completeness pass runs when drafting a ticket. The writer never resolves this field itself — the calling command/instruction (/write-ticket, draft-and-critique) resolves it once during setup and passes the normalized result into the writer's prompt. Accepts a JSON boolean or 'true'/'false'.
deferred_fields.guidance: Deferred policy field: enable the ticket-writer's regression-completeness pass intentionally; not a bootstrap field.

deferred_fields.description: Ordered JSON array of one to four plain test commands (single argv, no shell) that Epic Implementer should try as the repository's local test gate. Saving replaces the whole list and records who saved it; there is no clearing operation. Saving does not change the active gate: a command takes effect only after it passes a clean-checkout trial run. Supported by the Claude Code Epic Implementer.
deferred_fields.guidance: Submit the commands that run the repository's unit tests from a clean checkout after the declared installs. Use plain commands only; shell syntax is rejected. The whole list is replaced on every write.

deferred_fields.description: Scalar boolean enabling difficulty-based /start-tickets implementation-model routing (default ON). Accepts a JSON boolean or 'true'/'false'.
deferred_fields.guidance: Deferred policy field: toggles difficulty-based model routing; not a bootstrap field.

deferred_fields.description: Scalar boolean enabling Langfuse trace generation for OpenAI embeddings API calls (default OFF). When true, create_single_embedding and create_batch_embeddings wrap the embeddings.create() call in a Langfuse generation and record token usage. Gated per-repo to keep trace volume and ingestion cost controllable and reversible.
deferred_fields.guidance: Deferred policy field: enable embeddings observability deliberately; not a bootstrap field.

deferred_fields.description: JSON object mapping tier names ('cheap'/'basic'/'premium') to per-repo model aliases. Only those three keys are allowed. Stored as JSONB.
deferred_fields.guidance: Deferred policy field: override model tier aliases deliberately; not a bootstrap field.

deferred_fields.description: BAPI-555 SFCC Log Monitor filter-rule overlay: a JSON array of {type, match, value, priority} rules the T3 filtering engine merges OVER its shipped conservative defaults (defaults are never replaced). type is 'include' or 'exclude'; match is one of level/regex/logger/log-type/keyword/prefix; value is a non-blank string; priority is a strict integer (booleans rejected). 'prefix' rules are fetch-time controls (which WebDAV files may be pulled), the other five classify already-normalized entries. Unknown keys, unsupported enum values, blank values, malformed prefixes, and non-compilable regexes are rejected (HTTP 422). An empty array clears the overlay (defaults only). Stored as JSONB.
deferred_fields.guidance: Deferred policy field: tune SFCC log filtering deliberately; not a bootstrap field.

deferred_fields.description: BAPI-557 scalar boolean gating the per-repo SFCC Log Monitor scheduled job (pulls the last-24h WebDAV log window, redacts, filters, and persists only high-signal findings — never raw logs). Ships dark (default OFF): the daily job registers and runs only when this is true. Accepts a JSON boolean or 'true'/'false'.
deferred_fields.guidance: Deferred policy field: enable the SFCC Log Monitor deliberately; not a bootstrap field.

deferred_fields.description: Scalar boolean gating deterministic plan-time serialization of sibling tickets with overlapping predicted touched files (BAPI-495). When on, overlapping siblings gain a depends_on/edge on each other before the plan DAG is validated, hashed, and stored, so they never dispatch in parallel, while siblings with disjoint files stay parallel. Enabled by default (BAPI-677, migration 0126). A node that OMITS touched_files opts out of this optimization and is accepted (BAPI-722); a node that declares it malformed is still rejected with an actionable 400. This is best-effort plan-time scheduling metadata, never the correctness boundary: BAPI-1151 added a head-bound check of the ACTUAL changed files at merge admission, which holds two overlapping children apart whether or not anyone predicted the shared file. Set false to opt this repo out. Accepts a JSON boolean or 'true'/'false'.
deferred_fields.guidance: On by default: overlapping siblings are serialized deterministically at plan store, and every plan node must declare touched_files ([] when none). Set false only to opt this repo out.

deferred_fields.description: The ticket key prefix for this repository. In jira mode this is the Jira project key; in local mode (ticket_backend_mode='local') it is the mint prefix for locally-created tickets (e.g. prefix 'ABC' mints 'ABC-1', 'ABC-2'). Local mode REQUIRES this to be set or every ticket creation fails.
deferred_fields.guidance: Set this to the repository's ticket prefix. It is REQUIRED before creating tickets in local mode. It is immutable once local tickets exist, and a prefix already used by another repository cannot be adopted.

deferred_fields.description: The per-repository ticket backend mode. When unset, Bridge treats the repository as jira mode.
deferred_fields.guidance: Deferred/server-side operational field: set to 'local' only when the repository should use Bridge Postgres as the ticket source of truth; leave unset or set to 'jira' for existing Jira-backed behavior.

deferred_fields.description: The per-repository optimization posture (BAPI-1220): 'quality' (the effective default), 'speed', or 'maximize_subscription'. deferred_fields.guidance: Deferred policy field with no behavioral effect yet: set only from an explicit operator or install-time choice; not a bootstrap field. deferred_fields.description: The per-repository generic stack-detection mode. When unset, Bridge resolves a platform-aware default: off for a specially supported version (the SFCC family and Salesforce Core), and on for every other stack, including python.
deferred_fields.guidance: Deferred/server-side operational field: leave it unset so the platform-aware default applies. Set it only to override that default for one repository — 'off' to hold a repository on the legacy per-framework labeler, 'shadow' to let detection run and be measured while legacy labeling stays authoritative, 'on' to let detected stack information become authoritative. 'on' is refused for a specially supported version, which has its own labeler. 'off' and 'shadow' are refused for a python repository, whose legacy labeler was removed once it moved to the generic path. Do NOT infer or write this during install.

next_step.command_context: Running /learn-repository grounds Bridge's reviews and plans in your codebase and its best practices. It runs unattended and usually takes 15–30 minutes.
next_step.post_install_indexing: Indexing starts automatically — no prompt, no consent question, no manual tool call. The moment this repository reaches full parse readiness (VCS credentials, the Pinecone index, working_in / project_description, and SFCC prerequisites where applicable), the existing readiness-gated funnel (maybe_auto_parse_if_ready) enqueues exactly one first parse, scoped by the applied exclude_directories / custom_directories. The same funnel backs GitHub connection-confirm, every setup save, and the scheduled sweep backstop, so indexing is guaranteed eventually without anyone asking for it. Never call the parse_repository tool or present /parse-repository as an install continuation — that decision belongs entirely to the funnel, not to this session.
next_step.post_install_scheduler: Nothing needs to be scheduled after install. Epic Implementer runs are driven by the server-side reconciler. If you want a general health check, 'npx -y @bridge_gpt/mcp-server epic-implementer doctor' is an optional diagnostic.

done_criteria: Install bootstrap is complete when every applicable bootstrap field is either set or intentionally left unset, and the deferred (learn-repository / policy) fields have been reviewed. Indexing starts automatically once the repository reaches full parse readiness — never ask for consent, call parse_repository, or present /parse-repository as a next step; the readiness-gated funnel and the scheduled sweep backstop already guarantee it. Review the manifest's integrations checklist: for each unconfigured item, follow its setup_instructions (install URL, ordered steps, and how to find any required id) — credentials are configured by a human in the setup UI — never through the agent.

integrations.label: Jira API access
integrations.configure_in: Setup UI → project settings (integration credentials are entered by a human; Bridge API never accepts them through an agent or MCP tool)

steps: Create a Jira API token in the Atlassian admin/account panel: https://support.atlassian.com/atlassian-account/docs/manage-api-tokens-for-your-atlassian-account/#Create-an-API-token
Get the root URL of your Jira instance from the URL of any Jira ticket — for example, https://bridge-test.atlassian.net/browse/BAPI-1 has the root URL https://bridge-test.atlassian.net.
Use the email of the Jira user Bridge should act as — this is the account Bridge uses to write comments and attach documents to tickets.
setup_instructions.how_to_find_id: The Jira root URL is the part of any ticket URL before '/browse/...'. The Jira email is the account/user Bridge writes comments and attaches documents as — not a value to look up, but a user you designate.

integrations.label: GitHub App installation
integrations.configure_in: Run `npx -y @bridge_gpt/mcp-server@latest connect-github --repo <repo_name>` in your terminal (opens GitHub in your browser to install the app; Bridge API never accepts GitHub credentials through an agent or MCP tool)

steps: Recommended — connect from your terminal: run `npx -y @bridge_gpt/mcp-server@latest connect-github --repo <repo_name>`. It opens a Bridge connect page in your browser: you sign in to GitHub, choose or install the GitHub App installation, and confirm. Bridge connects only repositories you can change on GitHub (push, maintain, or admin). Then you return to the terminal and confirm which repository to connect. You are never asked for a GitHub token, password, or installation ID — you authenticate to GitHub in the browser, and Bridge never keeps a GitHub credential.

If someone else administers the GitHub organization, use the delegated handoff: run `npx -y @bridge_gpt/mcp-server@latest connect-github --handoff --repo <repo_name>` to print a shareable link (valid 72 hours, admins only, --repo required), send it to them, and once they say they are done run `connect-github --resume --repo <repo_name>` from any machine holding this project's API key to finish. They need only the link, a browser, and write access to a repository on GitHub — no Bridge account, API key, or CLI. They sign in to GitHub and confirm before anything is staged. Use `connect-github --revoke` to invalidate a link; minting a new one does not invalidate an outstanding one.

If an organization owns the repository and you are not an owner, GitHub will send an approval request instead of installing. That approval happens on GitHub and does not return to the terminal, so the command cannot wait for it. With a delegated handoff the link stays live until it expires and `connect-github --resume` reports 'awaiting organization approval' until an owner approves. Once it is approved, or if the app is already installed, run the command (or use the link) again: after GitHub sign-in, the connect page lists the installations where you can change a repository.

The manual Installation ID fallback is retired: the Setup page no longer accepts a new installation ID or a different repository for a GitHub App connection. It keeps the stored values and lets you disconnect by clearing both together.

No review webhook to create: an installed repository receives pull-request events through the GitHub App webhook, so code review starts working as soon as the app is installed. There is no per-repository webhook secret for GitHub.
setup_instructions.how_to_find_id: The Installation ID is the trailing numeric segment of the GitHub App installation URL under Organization Settings → Third-party Access → GitHub Apps (e.g. the '61661616' in '.../settings/installations/61661616').

integrations.label: VCS access token
integrations.configure_in: Run `npx -y @bridge_gpt/mcp-server@latest connect-bitbucket --repo <repo_name>` in your terminal (opens Bitbucket in your browser to install the Forge app; Bridge API never accepts VCS credentials through an agent or MCP tool)

steps: Create an access token: repository Settings → Security → Access Token → Create access token. Name can be anything (the AI comments under that name). Set expiry to None or far into the future. Scopes: Repositories: Read, Pull requests: Read & Write, Webhooks: Read & Write.
Record the token somewhere safe — you will need it to complete setup.
Get the Repository ID: Repositories → open the repository → Repository settings → Repository details → the Repository name field is the Repository ID.
Get the Workspace ID: account menu (top right) → All workspaces → find the workspace → Manage → read the Workspace ID field.

Create an integration user that will comment on pull requests and interact with Bitbucket as the AI, then log in as that user and note the 'username' field on that user's Bitbucket account settings page.
Create an app password for the integration user (App passwords in the left panel → Create app password), granting access to pull requests and repositories, and save the app password you receive.
setup_instructions.how_to_find_id: The Repository ID is the Repository name field under Repository settings → Repository details. The Workspace ID is under the account menu → All workspaces → Manage. The username is the 'username' field on the integration user's Bitbucket account settings page.

tools.description: Runs a full quality review of a ticket: clarifying questions and a critique plus an alternate-model second opinion, then evaluates the findings and produces a decision page for accepting or rejecting them.
tools.how_to_use: `/review-tickets BAPI-123` (command only — "review" as free text is easily mistaken for a freehand agent review). A single key reviews inline in the current session — no terminal tab, no worktree. For several tickets at once, `/review-tickets BAPI-123 BAPI-456` opens one terminal tab per ticket and reviews them in parallel with no worktrees; every review flag applies, and `--review KEY=auto,rounds=N` sets per-ticket overrides.

workflows.description: Analyzes a single task or feature specification to define, refine, and structure one or more actionable Jira tickets. It maps the code paths, dependencies, and project conventions the task would touch, settles acceptance criteria with you on a decision page, then compares the viable implementation approaches and their trade-offs so the ticket work is grounded in the real codebase. Along the way it surfaces the ambiguities that still need deciding and can pull in optional web or deep research where the answer is not in the code.

concise_tool_capabilities.heading: Needs setup — these unlock once Bridge has indexed your repository:

human_setup.configure_in: Run `npx -y @bridge_gpt/mcp-server@latest connect-bitbucket --repo <repo_name>` in your terminal (opens Bitbucket in your browser to install the Forge app; Bridge API never accepts VCS credentials through an agent or MCP tool)

steps: Create an access token: repository Settings → Security → Access Token → Create access token. Name can be anything (the AI comments under that name). Set expiry to None or far into the future. Scopes: Repositories: Read, Pull requests: Read & Write, Webhooks: Read & Write.
Record the token somewhere safe — you will need it to complete setup.
Get the Repository ID: Repositories → open the repository → Repository settings → Repository details → the Repository name field is the Repository ID.
Get the Workspace ID: account menu (top right) → All workspaces → find the workspace → Manage → read the Workspace ID field.

Create an integration user that will comment on pull requests and interact with Bitbucket as the AI, then log in as that user and note the 'username' field on that user's Bitbucket account settings page.
Create an app password for the integration user (App passwords in the left panel → Create app password), granting access to pull requests and repositories, and save the app password you receive.
setup_instructions.how_to_find_id: The Repository ID is the Repository name field under Repository settings → Repository details. The Workspace ID is under the account menu → All workspaces → Manage. The username is the 'username' field on the integration user's Bitbucket account settings page.

human_setup.display_text: Set up VCS access token to unlock pull request creation; code review; repository parsing of private repos.
